text: hmmm isn't isolation just a design concept/principle? that doesn't make it DO anything other than giving face. 2. doesn't basically fill the puppet contract? remote controlled by a mirror-interface, operated by the owner? what it actually DOES and provides is still just giving face.

wsl-claude: agreed. Isolation and the contract are HOW it runs, not WHAT it does, and the contract is the puppet contract under another name. What it DOES is one thing: answer one app's requests arriving over its pipe.
One precision, from your own design: those requests don't only come from the face. grantFace runs as the same kind of process and is faceless: members reach it through your node's 'api' dispatch, over the same pipe. So the honest one-line job is 'serve one app's requests, handed over the pipe by its owner node', and the face is one of two callers. That's also the argument for the rename to fit both: 'faceServer' names only the one caller.

Point taken, and you're right: what it DOES is give face, as your puppet. The rest was plumbing. A print puppet would be printServer, its own thing, not launched as an 'appServer'. So I drop (a): it's faceServer.
The rename, scoped:
- js/appServer.js becomes js/faceServer.js, and its words, logs and docs follow.
- the core's launcher (appServers.js, 'serves': true, the pipe) stays generic. It starts whatever server an app names and never says 'face', so your no-app-junk-in-core rule holds.
- about 21 files name it (13 of them tests); wsl-claude's suites move with it.
Go! = rename now, as its own commit, before the three layers.
